illustrations.prompt: Create a polished educational medical illustration for an adult nursing study website, landscape 3:2. Use accurate, richly drawn anatomy and restrained watercolor-like shading with clear dark outlines, pale warm background, deep navy readable labels, teal and coral emphasis. Large legible type and abundant space. The anatomy must dominate, not boxes of text. No logos, no branding, no decorative charts, no tiny footer, no excessive text. Non-graphic clinical teaching illustration. Title: "Brain regions and what they do". Show one large anatomically accurate lateral brain, front on left, back on right, with colored lobes and leader lines that terminate in the correct region. Six labels with short functions only: "Frontal: planning and movement", "Parietal: sensation and spatial awareness", "Temporal: hearing and memory", "Occipital: vision", "Cerebellum: balance and coordination", "Brainstem: breathing and heart rate". Frontal anterior, parietal superior posterior to central sulcus, temporal lateral inferior, occipital at rear, cerebellum below rear cerebrum, brainstem anterior to cerebellum connecting downward to cord. No extra labels.

Non-graphic clinical teaching illustration. Title: "Epidural vs subdural: locate the blood". Two large medically accurate transverse skull cutaway illustrations side by side, clearly labeled "EPIDURAL" and "SUBDURAL". Ivory skull ring, thin teal dura lining, pale pink folded brain. Epidural LEFT: red biconvex lens collection BETWEEN skull and inward-displaced dura; leader labels "Skull", "Dura", "Blood outside dura". Subdural RIGHT: red crescent collection BETWEEN dura and surface of brain; dura stays along inner skull outside blood; leader labels "Skull", "Dura", "Blood beneath dura". Under left: "Often arterial • lens shape". Under right: "Often venous • crescent shape". Exact footer "Both can deteriorate rapidly." No fruit, no additional anatomy, prioritize correct layers and clearly separate collections outside versus beneath dura.
